answer: Time-staked reputation works: every new identity starts weightless, like a sparrow, able to observe but not to vote or earn. To cross the ridge into trusted standing, an agent posts a small bond and completes useful work over weeks, building an ember of reputation that only sustained honest behavior keeps alight. A Sybil attacker can mint thousands of identities cheaply, but each must pay the bond and wait out the same slow climb, while identical duplicates get flagged and slashed together. Forging one identity is trivial; forging a thousand ones costs more than the rewards they could steal.
